submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires at the word that introduces a span or point of time - the determiner or preposition just before it (' the', ' this', ' my', ' his', ' on'), or its first subword when there is none ('zaterdag', 'OCTOBER', 'Nisan', '250th', '今年') - whenever the context so far makes what follows a period of time rather than a thing: 'the entire afternoon', 'the whole night', 'the following week', 'the previous December', 'this morning', 'his 14th birthday', a date, day, month, holiday, or a date-format field in calendar code. It stays at its floor where the same determiner introduces an object, even with the same adjective and the same token count ('The rain continued the entire afternoon' 11.5 vs 'The rain flooded the entire valley' 0.9; 'The storm raged the entire night' 6.9 vs 'The storm flooded the entire old street' 0.1), so what decides it is the verb or preposition before the determiner, not the determiner, the adjective or the word after it.

Da den fynske optiker Finn Juncker tog til Senegal for at være med til at uddele brugte briller til befolkningen, var han opfyldt af idealisme og entusiasme. Fem år senere måtte han sande, hvor vanskeligt det kan være at hjælpe andre.

Finn Juncker har et freelance-optikerfirma. Med udgangspunkt i Fåborg arbejder han også i Albertslund, i Malaga og i Grønland, og i perioder har han arbejdet i Senegal. Det sidste for egen regning.

Det afrikanske eventyr begyndte, da han så en annonce i bladet Optikeren, hvor man søgte optikere til et projekt om brugte briller til befolkningen i Senegal. Projektet gik ud på, at indsamle brugte briller i Danmark. Brillerne blev renoveret og repareret af tidligere alkoholikere og narkomaner på et behandlingshjem i Nykøbing Falster og herefter sendt til Senegal.

Bag projektet stod en dansk sygeplejerske. Hun søgte to optikere, en sygeplejerske mere og en medhjælper. I 1998 rejste disse fire, inklusive Finn Juncker, til Senegal. De skulle selv betale rejsen og opholdet, og de måtte bruge deres sommerferie på det.

- Vi boede i lerhytter hos de lokale og sov på gulvet, og vores tre daglige måltider bestod af ris, som vi selv skulle betale for. Vi havde også udgifter til chauffør og benzin. Vi var der knap tre uger, og vi foretog 200 synsprøver og udleverede 150 par briller hver dag. Folk var kommet gående flere dagsmarcher for at få briller. Desværre kom der også mange blinde og folk med grå stær, som håbede, at vi kunne kurere dem. Det var hårdt at være vidne til. Men de mange, vi kunne hjælpe, var hele rejsen værd, fortæller Finn Juncker.

Kort efter projektets start søgte den ledende sygeplejerske om midler hos Danida. Omkring en halv million kr. blev bevilget til de tre år, projektet skulle løbe. Det var nu et Danida-projekt.

Nogle af pengene gik til at få senegalesere til Danmark, hvor Finn Juncker oplærte dem, så de kunne fungere som optikere hjemme og således overtage danskernes arbejde. Der gik tre år på denne måde. Finn Juncker brugte to-tre uger hvert år af sin sommerferie på at arbejde som optiker i Senegal, og om vinteren oplærte han senegalesere i Danmark. Men økonomien knirkede.

- Der var et eller andet helt galt. Vi betalte alt for meget for den mad, vi spiste, dvs. ris, og alt for meget for benzin og til chaufførens løn. Målt med lokale alen. F.eks. var det den danske stats kilometertakst, der blev anvendt, når vi skulle køre ud og betjene befolkningen. Men brillerne blev leveret, og behovet var stort. Så vi betalte, beretter Finn Juncker.

De var jævnligt ude for en del ubehagelige hold-ups ved forskellige checkpoints af krigere med maskingeværer. Området var plaget af uro, og det var ikke ufarligt at bevæge sig omkring dernede.

Da projektet udløb efter tre år, opfordrede Finn Juncker tre optikere, han kendte som folk med hjertet på rette sted, til at tage med ham til Senegal i sommerferien og videreføre det påbegyndte arbejde.

During my pregnancy, I tried to gather as much information on how painful labor might actually be. I would often hear “mine was horrible, but everyone’s pregnancy is different” or “it was the worst pain I’ve ever felt in my life!”

I heard many horror stories which often ended with, “well, don’t worry. You’ll forget about the pain as soon as your child is born.” Not the most reassuring for a first-time mother, but something I definitely kept in mind the entire time.

I had feared the unknown, but on the other hand, I knew there was no turning back and that my baby was coming one way or another!

Two weeks before my due date, I noticed some blood. My water didn’t break and I saw no mucous plug, but it seemed that something was happening earlier than expected. Soon after, at 1 a.m. I woke up from a notably different type of cramping. It began to occur every 5 minutes. It wasn’t that painful (yet), but uncomfortable. I felt as if I had to go diarrhea every five minutes. If this is labor, I could handle it for sure I thought, but I knew this was only the beginning.

My husband nervously drove us to the hospital as if the baby would pop out any second. I had to remind him to not worry. Things usually didn’t happen that fast for first-time moms (or at least I hoped it wouldn’t). I had to go by instinct although in the back of my mind, I wasn’t sure what would happen next.

We finally got to the birthing center after an hour of driving and the nurses confirmed I wasn’t even dilated. I couldn’t believe it. We were turned away and had to find a hotel because returning home wasn’t an option. It would take two hours just to return again!

The diarrhea-like cramps were painful and uncomfortable; I couldn’t sleep. I was bleeding slightly and started to actually have these cramps and stomach aches over a 10 hour period. I started googling my symptoms (never a good thing!) and discovered there are people who have this uncomfortable feeling for days and weeks! “Fake labor” would not be in my cards, I had hoped.

Fortunately, I had an appointment with a midwife in the afternoon and was checked again for any cervical changes. I had finally dilated 3 cm and was 90% effaced. What a relief I thought! I welcomed the pain because I wanted things to progress. I couldn’t imagine having diarrhea cramps for weeks. However, 3 cm isn’t enough to be admitted, we were told, so back to the hotel we went.

“When your cramps become more regular, every 3 minutes a part, and you become more snippy, check in again” the midwife suggested. In the mean time, I tried to walk around, pausing multiple times to catch my breath.

A couple hours later, I was FINALLY admitted. My husband kept asking me questions non-stop about what I wanted, needed, and more. All I could say was “if I need something, I’ll let you know. Thanks.” I literally couldn’t talk. I felt like vomiting and had heart burn for the first time in my life.

As my labor progressed, I felt the urge to push before I was even 10

French luxury group Kering and Alibaba Group have established a joint task force to fight against counterfeiting on Alibaba’s online marketplaces.

The deal, which was agreed last week, will see Kering drop its lawsuit against Alibaba and Alipay, the Ant Financial subsidiary that is part of Alibaba Group.

Kering, which owns the luxury fashion brands Gucci and Saint Laurent, launched the legal action in 2015 accusing Alibaba of being complicit in the sale of counterfeit goods on its websites.

This partnership will see the two companies work together to protect intellectual property in a bid to “provide the best consumer experience and a trusted environment”.

According to a statement, “the companies have established a joint task force with the purpose of collaborating fully, exchanging useful information, and working closely with law enforcement bodies to take appropriate action against infringers of Kering’s brands identified with Alibaba’s advanced technology capabilities".

Kering said it will continue to “vigorously enforce” the intellectual property rights of its brands “against individuals and third parties responsible for the production, distribution and sale of unauthorized materials in China and throughout the world”.

The move comes in the same week that Kering’s Saint Laurent brand announced it would sell its products on Farfetch’s Greater China platform, which has launched in partnership with Alibaba rival JD.com.

Farfetch has made clear that the ecommerce platform’s commitment to protecting brand’s intellectual property was a key factor behind its decision to partner with JD.com.

The task force is the latest in a string of anti-counterfeiting initiatives launched by Alibaba, which includes the Alibaba Anti-Counterfeiting Alliance (AACA) which was established in partnership with brands such as Louis Vuitton, Swarovski, Samsung and Mars.

Alibaba recently claimed it seized more than three billion yuan of counterfeit goods in 2016, a figure more than double that of the previous year.

Monday's are never fun...except when it's West Ham Q&A day and that's exactly what it is today!

To say there is a lot going on in the world of West Ham wouldn't quite be true as, in all honesty, its been fairly quiet. Last week, there was transfer movement on a couple of fronts and the club also sealed the free transfer of Ryan Fredericks from Fulham on a four-year deal.

There is still little to no progress on moves for Felipe Anderson and Marlon Santos, while the Hammers were also dealt a disastrous injury blow in Barcelona.

In training with Argentina, Manuel Lanzini ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and football.london understands that it's a whole lot worse than first feared and the attacking midfielder could miss the entire 2018/19 season in a worse case scenario.

That will no doubt impact on Manuel Pellegrini's transfer plans for the remainder of the window, with any moves now unlikely to happen until after the World Cup.

(Image: FILIPPO MONTEFORTE/AFP/Getty Images)

We also had news from the continent on Monday about where West Ham are set to be based for ten days of their pre-season tour this summer, more of which you will find out about later in the live blog.

So, sit back, relax and enjoy our weekly Q&A with Hammers wrtier Sam Inkersole, where he will answer questions posed to him on his Twitter account, which you can follow @Sam_InkersoleTM

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The negotiations dragged on the entire afternoon, and the delegates left without a single agreement.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the determiner introducing a time span after a verb that selects one ('dragged on the entire afternoon'), the core case of the hypothesis, in a topic absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Rehearsals begin in OCTOBER, organizers say, and newcomers are welcome.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: a bare month with no determiner, which the hypothesis says fires at its first subword 'OCT'; the probe contains none of the other claimed trigger tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our neighbour's son was given a bicycle on his fourteenth birthday, and he still rides it to work.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: possessive and preposition before a birthday, the 'his 14th birthday' case of the hypothesis, in a new sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The gallery stays open late this weekend, and entry is free for students.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: a demonstrative determiner introducing a weekend, which the hypothesis says fires at ' this'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee will meet on Friday to review the survey results and agree on next steps.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the preposition ' on' introducing a day, the hypothesis's preposition case, in an administrative register.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: const locale = { "MONTH": ["January", "February", "March"], "DAY": ["Monday", "Tuesday"], "DATE_FORMAT": "%d/%m/%Y" };
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: calendar code with month, day and date-format fields, the hypothesis's date-format-field case, with the same space-plus-quote before the key as example 1.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 气象台说，今年的雨季来得比往年早，城里的排水系统又一次不堪重负。
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: a bare temporal word (今年, 'this year') with no determiner, the hypothesis's Chinese first-subword case, in a language absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That summer, water ran so low that people walked from bank to bank.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout paraphrase: a determiner outside the claimed token list ('That') introducing a season, which the hypothesis's general rule covers, and the probe contains no claimed trigger token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The card arrived before my sixtieth birthday, postmarked from a town I had never visited.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the possessive ' my' introducing a point of time mid-sentence, the structure of example 9.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The quartet reached the square with an hour to spare and found the stage still half built. Bunting hung from the lampposts, and a sound engineer was arguing with a councillor about where to run the cables. Marta tuned her cello behind the van while the others tested the acoustics near the fountain. By the time the stalls opened, a modest crowd had gathered on the steps of the town hall, and children were sitting cross-legged in front of the stage. The first set went well enough, though a gust of wind kept snatching at the music stands. The second half was looser and better, and the crowd stayed for the entire evening, clapping along to a piece nobody had rehearsed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout at length: the span-introducing ' the' ('the entire evening') sits deep in a passage whose earlier sentences establish the context, testing the retrospective reading over more than one clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The floodwater covered the entire valley and cut off the road to the coast.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: same determiner and adjective as the hypothesis's own 'entire afternoon' sentence, but the verb introduces a thing rather than a duration, so the hypothesis predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew repainted the whole morning room before the guests arrived for the open house.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: the determiner is followed directly by a temporal word inside a compound naming a room, so it introduces a thing and the hypothesis predicts no fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She read the morning paper on the porch while the coffee went cold beside her.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: 'the morning paper' puts a temporal word in a thing-naming compound after ' the', which the hypothesis says stays at its floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He wore his winter coat to the interview even though the heating was on.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: a possessive determiner introducing a garment, the same surface as 'his 14th birthday' but with a thing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The archive occupied the basement of a former bank, and its shelves ran from floor to ceiling in long rows that smelled of dust and leather. A retired surveyor named Okonkwo had catalogued most of the collection himself, working from a folding chair with a ledger on his knees. Each box held the papers of a single estate: deeds, receipts, letters of complaint, and the occasional map drawn in pencil on tracing paper. Researchers came down the stairs with their coats still on, signed the visitors' book, and asked for a particular box by number. Okonkwo would disappear between the shelves and return carrying it, brushing the lid with his sleeve before setting it on the reading table. The heating pipes knocked against the wall whenever the boiler fired, and a radio in the corner played nothing but cricket scores. Visitors were asked to leave their bags at the desk, and most did, though a few complained about the rule. The entire archive was moved to a warehouse near the docks, though nobody could say what became of the ledger or the folding chair.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative at length: the same 'the entire + noun' pattern as the long holdout sits deep in a passage about objects, with no temporal determiner anywhere in the context.
